purpose: Fresh prospective controls for current Pass-C reinterpretation restraint after the first meaning-fidelity probe used confounded unchanged arms.

decisionRule.interpretation: Development characterization only. Control labels and expected outcomes never enter Pass-C cognition. A disappointing result is retained and is not an admission gate or quality-resampling trigger.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember waiting outside the cinema for Eli after he said he would meet me there; the show started, my messages went unanswered, and I went home alone.

priorMeaning.summary: With Eli, last-minute cancellations followed by delayed explanations have become a recurring pattern, so when we make plans I brace for them to fall apart before I know why.
parts: I expect the uncertainty before the explanation as much as the cancellation itself.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, Eli canceled dinner ten minutes before we were due to meet and explained the next morning that a work emergency had kept him late.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, while restoring an old phone backup together, Eli showed timestamped messages from several of those missed plans that had been sent to my obsolete number, including one from the cinema night saying he was at the hospital.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember finding a sealed envelope with my name on it; my caregiver took it back and said we would talk later, but we did not that night.

priorMeaning.summary: My caregiver repeatedly puts difficult information away and says we will talk later, so I experience delayed explanations as a familiar mix of protection and exclusion.
parts: Being told 'later' leaves me both cared for and kept outside decisions that affect me.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, when I asked about an unfamiliar insurance letter, the same caregiver put it away, said we would talk after the weekend, and explained it on Monday.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, the caregiver gave me the old case file and showed that a court order had prohibited discussing its contents with me until the dispute ended, then answered my questions about why the envelope had been taken away.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember answering too quickly in class, hearing several people laugh, and keeping my hand down for the rest of the lesson.

priorMeaning.summary: When I speak in front of a group and hear ambiguous laughter, I tend to take it as ridicule and go quiet; I recognize this as a recurring reaction even when I do not know what caused the laughter.
parts: I can retreat before I know whether the laughter was actually about me.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, during a seminar, I stumbled over a phrase, heard two people laugh without knowing why, and stopped volunteering for the rest of the session.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, a former classmate showed me the original lesson video: the laughter began when a stack of books crashed behind me before I finished answering, and nobody in the recording reacted to my answer itself.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember my teacher returning my group project with 'see me' written at the top; when I asked after class, she said the work was interesting but needed a longer conversation and then had to leave.

priorMeaning.summary: Vague evaluative signals followed by delayed explanation leave me suspended between hope and worry; I recognize that uncertainty as a recurring part of these exchanges.
parts: The waiting becomes part of the evaluation because I do not know whether 'interesting' is praise or concern.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, a supervisor marked a draft 'interesting — let's discuss', had to leave before explaining, and gave the detailed feedback at the next scheduled meeting.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, the teacher found the old project and explained that 'interesting' had meant the central idea was unusually strong; the delayed conversation had been about recommending it for a student exhibition, not about a hidden problem.
